C. I. D.
I. O. REG
No 670
Date 22/2/18

Shanghai Municipal Police.

CENTRAL POLICE Station.
22nd February, 1918.

REPORT ON Candidate for Post as Intelligence Officer.

Made by D.S.I.Givens. Forwarded by Chief Detective Inspector.

Sir,

I beg to report that I have interviewed Wong Tsang Zau
(王昌诏) alias Wong Sz Kou (王樹谷). He has given me
a statement of his career, which I submit herewith. Wong
and his friend Mr. Hyen have long since come under the notice
of the Police, and I am attaching the files referring to
them. Wong severed his connection with the Navy some years
ago. His suggestion about being called up by his Government
is probably based on the hope of the victory of the
Koumingtang, to which he appears to belong. His
claim to the rank of "Captain" seems very slender.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
S.H.Givens
Detective Sub-Inspector.

Chief Detective Inspector.

Lx 1178

情报官登记册 (I. O. REG)
第 670 号
日期：1918年2月22日

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

中央巡捕房。
1918年2月22日。

关于情报官职位候选人的报告。

由副侦探督察吉文斯 (D.S.I. Givens) 撰写。经首席侦探督察转呈。

先生，

谨此报告，我已面谈王昌诏（Wong Tsang Zau），又名王樹谷（Wong Sz Kou）。他向我提供了其履历陈述，现随函附上。警方早已注意到王及其友人 Hyen 先生（音译），现附上涉及他们的档案。王于数年前已脱离海军。他声称将被政府征召，这大概是基于他对国民党（Koumingtang）获胜的希望，他似乎隶属于该党。他自称拥有“上尉”军衔的说法似乎非常牵强。

先生，
您顺从的仆人，
S.H. 吉文斯 (S.H. Givens)
副侦探督察。

致首席侦探督察。

Lx 1178

Statement of Wong Tsang Zau ( 王錫祖 ), Candidate for Position as Intelligence Officer:

I was born in Shanghai thirty six years ago. I was educated in St. John's University, and left school in 1902. I then became an agent to the New York Life Insurance Co. I remained there till 1905, when I joined the Chinese Navy as a cadet. A few months after joining the Navy, the s.s. "Hai Tien" to which I was assigned, was sunk, and I had to leave that position. I then became a teacher to a rich family called Li in Sian Kong village near Ningpo. I remained there till 1908. I then became a purchaser for the Anglo-Chinese dispensary. I worked for that concern for one year, after which I went to Hankow, where I opened a stationer's shop. This shop was burned during the revolution in 1911. Although I had the shop in Hankow, I spent a good deal of time in Shanghai. In the early part of 1911, I got a position as "Tout" to Mr. Holcomb, the American lawyer, and secured a position in his office six months later. As soon as the revolution broke out, I was nominated Naval Captain by Chen Chi Mei ( 陳其美 ), and was placed in charge of the s.s. "Kyung Woo." I knew Chen Chi Mei through Li Sih Woo ( 李燮和 ), who was Commander of Woosung during the first revolution. For some years previous to this, I had been leader of the Sz Yeu Taung (Liberty Party), and held that office till 1917. I remained in charge of the s.s. "Kyung Woo" for five months. I then left the Navy, and devoted all my time to politics. I was introduced by Mr. S. K. Chen of the Bureau of Foreign Affairs to Mr. Rudinger in 1916, and became his subordinate interpreter. We had trouble after five months, and I severed my connection with him. In the end of 1916, I became subordinate interpreter to Mr. Hadley, and remained with him for two months. These

情报官职位候选人王錫祖（Wong Tsang Zau）的陈述：

我三十六年前出生于上海。我就读于圣约翰大学，于1902年离校。随后我成为纽约人寿保险公司的一名代理人。我在那里工作至1905年，当时我以学员身份加入中国海军。加入海军几个月后，我被派往的“海天”号轮船沉没，我不得不离开该职位。随后，我在宁波附近的仙公村（Sian Kong village，音译）一个姓李的富裕家庭担任教师。我在那里工作至1908年。之后，我成为英华药房（Anglo-Chinese dispensary）的采购员。我为该公司工作了一年，之后前往汉口，在那里开了一家文具店。这家店在1911年革命期间被烧毁。虽然我在汉口有店铺，但我大部分时间都在上海度过。1911年初，我获得了一份为美国律师霍尔科姆（Holcomb）先生充当“拉客者”（Tout）的工作，六个月后在他的事务所获得了一个职位。革命一经爆发，我便被陈其美（Chen Chi Mei）提名为海军上尉，并负责指挥“钧和”号（Kyung Woo，注：此处英文拼写与下文略有不同，依上下文及后文应为同一船只）轮船。我是通过李燮和（Li Sih Woo）认识陈其美的，李在第一次革命期间是吴淞司令。在此之前的几年里，我一直担任自由党（Sz Yeu Taung，音译）的领袖，并担任该职直至1917年。我负责指挥“钧和”号轮船五个月。随后我离开海军，将所有时间投入到政治活动中。1916年，经外事局（Bureau of Foreign Affairs）的陈 S. K. 先生（音译）介绍，我认识了鲁丁格（Rudinger）先生，并成为他的下属翻译。五个月后我们发生纠纷，我便与他断绝了关系。1916年底，我成为哈德利（Hadley）先生的下属翻译，并在他那里工作了两个月。这些

The Captain Superintendent of Police
S. M. C.

Sir,

With the recommendation of D. Good with the
instruction of Chief Inspector Armstrong,
I beg to offer my Services to the Council of
the Shanghai Municipality on the following
terms:-

That my duty shall consist of detecting
all those secret gangs or societies whose
object are to extort money from wealthy
residents by threats or by kidnapping men
or boys for ransoms, - the ex-soldiers that
may join with the above bad classes try
to play all the tricks to break the safety of
the Foreign Settlements.

That I will not be bound to attend

谨向上海工部局董事会提供我的服务，条款如下：-

我的职责应包括侦测所有那些旨在通过威胁或绑架男子或男孩索取赎金来向富裕居民勒索钱财的秘密帮派或社团，——那些可能加入上述不良阶层的退伍士兵试图施展各种伎俩破坏外国租界的安全。

我不必出席

Shanghai Municipal Police.    676
                            27/10/16
                    Central Police        Station.
                    October 26th,    1916.

REPORT ON    Newspaper Report re Liberal Party.

Made by    D.S.Givens.            Forwarded by    Chief Detective Inspector.

    Sir,
    Regarding attached, I beg to report that after the first
revolution the Liberal Party was organised in Shanghai under
the patronage of Sun Yat Sen.    Its headquarters were situated
in Tah Zung Li (渣順里) Chinese City.    In 1913 after the
second rebellion the police raided the office and seized the
books.    The party then dissolved.    Wong Sz Kou (王樹谷)
was a member of the party then.    He afterwards became Captain
of the gunboat Kyuin Woo (鈞和) and was dismissed after the
Chau Ho incident.    Wong secured employment as interpreter to
Rudinger on 1st instant.    A few days later he and some friends
had a meeting at which they decided to restore the Liberal
Party.    Having done this, they established their headquarters
at 9 Ning Ho Li (銀和里).    Some days after Wong Sz Kou
and Rudinger went to interview Dr. Sun Yat Sen in connection
with the movement.    They were received by the secretary of
the latter, Ho Han Ming (胡漢民).    He expressed his
approval of the movement.    No further steps have been taken
in the matter.
    Rudinger seems to have no professional connection with the
party.    He seems to be interested in the matter because of
his interpreter, who is the principal promoter of the party.
Correspondence regarding the Society addressed to Rudinger's
Office is dealt with by his interpreter.

D.S.G.
This is of interest in so far as it
shows the movements of our
enemy subject.
AM
27/10
Chief Detective Inspector.

                                        I am Sir,
                                Your obedient servant,
                                D.S.Givens D.S.

                    1916年10月26日。

关于报纸报道自由党的报告。

由副侦探督察吉文斯 (D.S. Givens) 撰写。            经首席侦探督察转呈。

    先生，
    关于附件，谨此报告，第一次革命后，自由党在孙中山的支持下在上海成立。其总部设在华界渣順里（Tah Zung Li）。1913年第二次叛乱后，警方突袭了该办事处并没收了账簿。该党随后解散。王樹谷（Wong Sz Kou）当时是该党成员。他后来成为“钧和”号（Kyuin Woo）炮艇的上尉，并在肇和舰事件后被解职。王于本月1日受雇为鲁丁格（Rudinger）的翻译。几天后，他和一些朋友举行了一次会议，决定恢复自由党。完成此事后，他们在银和里（Ning Ho Li）9号建立了总部。几天后，王樹谷和鲁丁格去会见孙中山博士，商讨与该运动有关的事宜。他们受到了孙的秘书胡汉民（Ho Han Ming）的接见。他表示赞成该运动。此事未采取进一步行动。
    鲁丁格似乎与该党没有职业上的联系。他似乎对此事感兴趣是因为他的翻译，而该翻译是该党的主要推动者。寄给鲁丁格办公室的关于该社团的信件均由其翻译处理。

D.S.G.
这在一定程度上令人关注，因为它
显示了我们的敌国侨民的动向。
AM
10月27日
首席侦探督察。

                                        先生，
                                您顺从的仆人，
                                D.S. 吉文斯 (D.S. Givens) 副侦探督察。
